title: LoRA meets Riemannion: Muon Optimizer for Parametrization-independent Low-Rank Adapters
claim: Across a sweep of learning rates, our method gives a better trade-off between two quality metrics than the baseline.
layout: single scatter plot with legend on right, two-metric trade-off
description: A single scatter plot with text similarity (TS) on the x-axis (about 0.315 to 0.335) and image similarity (IS) on the y-axis (about 0.47 to 0.68). The y-axis labels appear in non-monotonic order, which is likely a plotting quirk. Blue dots show LoRA at four learning rates (2e-5 to 2e-4). Orange dots show the proposed method at four learning rates (5e-6 to 4e-5). Marker size grows with learning rate. A gridded legend to the right lists each run. Orange points sit above or to the right of the matching blue points. This suggests the method gives a better trade-off between image and text fidelity at each learning-rate setting. The eye goes first to the colored clusters along the diagonal trade-off front.
caption: Comparison of text and image similarities for LoRA and our method with rank 4 at different learning rates on 400 step.
abstract: This work presents a novel, fully Riemannian framework for Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) that geometrically treats low-rank adapters by optimizing them directly on the fixed-rank manifold. This formulation eliminates the parametrization ambiguity present in standard Euclidean optimizers. Our framework integrates three key components to achieve this: (1) we derive Riemannion, a new Riemannian optimizer on the fixed-rank matrix manifold that generalizes the recently proposed Muon optimizer; (2) we develop a Riemannian gradient-informed LoRA initialization, and (3) we provide an efficient implementation without prominent overhead that uses automatic differentiation to compute arising geometric operations while adhering to best practices in numerical linear algebra. Comprehensive experimental results on both LLM and diffusion model architectures demonstrate that our approach yields consistent and noticeable improvements in convergence speed and final task performance over both standard LoRA and its state-of-the-art modifications.
